verdict.rationale: Crossplane says it extends Kubernetes RBAC to everything it orchestrates and exposes declarative APIs that "humans, automation, and AI systems can safely act on". Community comments add that users are granted permission only at the interface they interact with, which supports least-privilege scoping of what an agent may do. However, nothing in the evidence documents actually issuing scoped credentials (tokens, service accounts, keys) to an agent. The capability appears to rely on underlying Kubernetes mechanisms that the evidence never describes. Missing for 10: a documented workflow for issuing per-agent credentials, credential scoping/expiry/rotation details, agent-specific permission guidance, and independent hands-on corroboration.
